content_of_post_to_comment: Years ago, “which one?” was a common critique against religion. This was a frequent New Atheist line. Since there’s so much disagreement, it was said, the sensible posture is agnosticism or atheism. Lately I’ve had the opposite intuition. What’s striking is the convergence: >70% of the world is either Abrahamic or Dharmic. There are still choices to be made. This isn’t an “all paths are really the same” sort of observation. But, I think the intuition which “which one?” plays off is misleading.
comment: Maybe “which one?” mistakes disagreement within a broad family of traditions for evidence against the family itself. But convergence only gets us to a shared starting point; it doesn't tell us which differences matter most.
